subject: Prospect Q&A: inference execution locations, subprocessors, retention & deletion
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@healthspan.io>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Qs on where data is processed and deletion timeline

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — HealthSpan is excited about Redwood's latency and cost profile. Before we move deeper on evaluation I need to get a concise answer from your team on a few compliance items we track for our security review: 

1) In which cloud regions and countries is inference executed for the hosted Redwood API by default?
2) Who are the subprocessors involved (cloud providers, CDNs, analytics) and in which regions do they operate?
3) If requests are routed cross-border (e.g., EU->US), what triggers that routing and do you persist any copies outside the requested region?
4) What's the retention timeline for request payloads, logs, and cached KV state? Can customers shorten/disable retention?
5) If a customer requests data deletion or account termination, what is the deletion workflow and typical time-to-erasure?

Can you please provide a short Q&A or point me to the relevant evidence pack? Attaching our intake form for reference (we may share with procurement).

Best,
Sara
Senior Security Manager
HealthSpan Labs

Subject: RE: Quick Qs on where data is processed and deletion timeline — concise answers + evidence

Hi Sara (and Tom),

Thanks for the specific list — below is a compact Q&A and we've attached the residency diagram, current subprocessor inventory and our SOC2 summary for your security team. If you need a formal attestation or a signed addendum on data locality we can provide a standard clause for your legal team.

Q1 — Inference execution regions (hosted API default):
- Default routing: requests are routed to the region closest to the request origin by latency and capacity. For customers on the hosted plan, our common execution regions are US East (aws/us-east-1), US West (aws/us-west-2), EU West (gcp/europe-west1) and APAC (gcp/asia-southeast1).
- Dedicated/Private: customers can pin capacity to a single region or private VPC (on-prem) to guarantee execution locality.

Q2 — Subprocessors and operating regions (short list):
- AWS (compute & storage): us-east-1, us-west-2 (primary serving + object store)
- Google Cloud (edge serving, analytics): europe-west1, asia-southeast1
- Fastly / Cloud CDN (optional CDN for static assets): global POPs, no request payload caching by default
- Datadog (metrics/traces): US & EU tenants depending on customer region
- HashiCorp Vault (secrets, KMS integrations): hosted in US; customers can bring own KMS/HSM for Private.

Q3 — Cross-border routing and persistence:
- Triggers: routing changes when (a) the customer request originates from a different region, (b) nearest-region capacity is saturated and policy allows cross-region failover, or (c) customer explicitly configures multi-region fallback.
- Persistence: we do not replicate customer request payloads across regions for hosted customers by default. Transient KV cache or model cache may exist on serving nodes in the region that executed the request. When cross-region failover occurs, we only route live requests — we do not asynchronously replicate full customer payload archives across regions unless a customer enables multi-region replication.

Q4 — Retention timelines and controls:
- Request payloads (hosted): default retention 30 days; logs/trace metadata retained 90 days for troubleshooting/SLAs.
- KV/prefix cache (serving nodes): ephemeral; cache entries live only on serving nodes and are evicted based on LRU and TTL. No long-term persistent storage of raw inputs in caches.
- Customer controls: customers can request reduced retention or disable non-essential logging via account settings or by contract for Dedicated/Private plans.

Q5 — Deletion workflow and typical time-to-erasure:
- Self-serve deletion: account admin can request data deletion in Console — initiates automated deletion job.
- Backend process: deletion job enqueues tasks for object store blobs, index entries, logs, and analytics pointers. We verify deletion via checksums and internal audit logs.
- SLA: standard hosted deletion completes within 30 days of request. For Dedicated/Private with contractual terms we can agree a shorter window (e.g., 7–14 days) and provide deletion certificates.

Additional notes on auditability & evidence:
- Audit logs: we provide request-level audit traces (timestamp, model, route, latency) for 90 days by default. Longer retention available as a paid add-on.
- KMS & encryption: all data at rest is encrypted; customers may use our managed keys or integrate with their KMS for Private deployments.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report available (attached); we can also coordinate an in-scope questionnaire exchange or provide a dedicated security review call.

Attachments: residency-diagram.png, subprocessor-inventory.csv, SOC2-summary.pdf

If you'd like, we can also create a one-page table specifically mapping HealthSpan's regulator list to our evidence items. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if teams prefer to review live.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference

Thanks Monica — this is really helpful. A couple of quick clarifications before we share with our InfoSec: 

1) KV/prefix cache: can you confirm whether any of the cache keys or values are written to durable object storage during the eviction/flush cycle?
2) Cross-region failover: when failover is triggered for latency/capacity, are there any downstream analytics or monitoring pipelines that pull raw request payloads to another region?

If the answers are both no (no durable writes, no cross-region payload pulls), we're in good shape for our initial security review.

Best,
Sara
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@healthspan.io>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: RE: Quick Qs on where data is processed and deletion timeline — concise answers + evidence

Hi Sara — short answers: no and no.

Details:
- Cache persistence: KV/prefix caches are in-memory or stored on ephemeral NVMe attached to the serving host. Eviction does not trigger durable object-store writes of raw request payloads. Diagnostic snapshots we capture for debugging are redacted and limited to trace metadata, not full payload.
- Analytics/monitoring: our analytics pipelines ingest metrics and traces (ids, timings, error codes). We do not forward raw request payloads to analytics or monitoring systems. In the rare case a full payload is required for debugging (customer-approved), we route a staged extraction to the region requested and purge after customer confirmation; such access is logged and requires a ticket.

We can add explicit language to a data processing addendum (DPA) to reflect these commitments if HealthSpan requires it. Let me know and I will prepare a draft.

Thanks,
Monica
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
